headline: AI market flooded with Jev-like decision models after researcher claims TypeSafe copied their work
summary: ConvAI Innovations founder Nandakishor Mukkunnoth alleges TypeSafe's Jev architecture, a novel decision model API, was based on his earlier research. This has sparked a debate as similar models from major players emerge.
details: TypeSafe's Jev, a novel decision model API, has seen a surge of competitors and open-source projects from major players like Microsoft and OpenAI. However, Nandakishor Mukkunnoth of ConvAI Innovations claims he developed the core architecture for Jev over a year prior to its release. This has raised questions about intellectual property in the rapidly evolving AI market.

Jev and its clones function as APIs for decision models, designed to be integrated into existing codebases. Users provide input data, such as customer transactions, along with specific questions like "is the user looking for a return?" The AI then provides probability estimates for yes/no or multiple-choice answers.

This practical application is considered novel because it neatly bypasses common issues associated with traditional large language models (LLMs). Jev-like models avoid token-by-token text generation, conversational history, extensive context feeding, and conversational hallucination. They offer direct data in the form of probabilities, making them exceptionally fast and cost-effective compared to standard LLMs.

TypeSafe released Jev alongside a brief description of its "System One" architecture. Days later, Mukkunnoth detailed in a blog post that he had "designed the Jev architecture one year back," referencing his arXiv paper "SalesRLAgent," published March 30, 2025. This paper described his probability estimation model, including published model weights and dataset, followed by a more aligned paper in September.

Mukkunnoth expressed frustration at being overlooked, attributing it to his "vertical use case" approach with SalesRLAgent, which focused on a specific problem. In contrast, TypeSafe positioned Jev as a general-purpose decision engine, releasing it as a complete, hosted product with its own servers, API, documentation, developer kits, and pricing structure.

Despite his initial bitterness, Mukkunnoth chose to release the open-source Laya, a Jev-style model and interface, around the same time. Laya can be run on local hardware and supports multiple languages. Both TypeSafe and Mukkunnoth notably named their models "System 1/One" types, likely referencing Daniel Kahneman's "Thinking, Fast and Slow."

The hype around this new AI application quickly led to a wave of similar services. Within weeks of Jev's release, Microsoft launched "Microsoft Decision," OpenAI introduced "OpenAI Decisions API," and Fastino unveiled "Glide." Cloudflare's "Clef" and Perplexity's "Decider" also arrived with open weights, allowing users to run them on their own systems.

The open-source community also saw an explosion of alternatives, including Amazon's "Strands Decider 2B," Kev, Von, Jeff, jevlike, SemIf, OpenJev, NanoJev, and Ollaya. Many of these projects, commercial and open-source, share a common root: adapting existing lightweight models, often variants of Alibaba's Qwen, with additional layers for input, output, and decision procedures. Mukkunnoth's Laya, however, is based on encoder-only models from the Bert family. The rapid proliferation suggests that many might have drawn inspiration from earlier work.

summary: A practical guide to choosing the best free AI API for your project in 2024. It compares OpenRouter, Together.ai, and Groq, all offering generous free tiers for development and small production workloads.
details: A practical guide to choosing the right free AI API for your project in 2024. The article compares three major free-tier providers: OpenRouter, Together.ai, and Groq.
OpenRouter is recommended for maximum flexibility, offering access to over 50 models with one API key. It's best for projects needing model variety and easy switching.
Groq is highlighted for speed-critical paths, while Together.ai is suggested for volume and consistent performance with a good selection of open-source models.
All three platforms provide generous free tiers. These tiers are sufficient for both development and small production workloads, saving time and money.
